data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject only if a failure of the subject would make the test itself fail before any assertion can pass, and it merely describes the subject when the test can pass independently of whether the subject's mutation is caught; the 3-of-26 result is a confound of one repository, one author, one week, and the fact that the mutations were proposed by models that had read the acceptance record.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the same result were reproduced across multiple repositories and authors, the confound would be weakened.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the mutations were proposed by a model that had not seen the acceptance record, the distribution might change.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the guards were randomized across mutation types, the constraining relation could be measured independently.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The constraining relation is causal: the subject's failure must be a necessary condition for the test's failure. In the observed record, the small sample size and single-author artifacts make it impossible to separate the guard's constraining force from the author's expectations.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
